kurz: Baking soda is alkaline. It raises batter together with acid, speeds up browning and softens plant cells.
bild_im_kopf: Like an accelerator pedal for several processes at once: browning, softening, rising. That is why a pinch is always enough.
was_passiert: Baking soda raises the [[ph-wert|pH]]. In alkaline conditions, browning and the breakdown of [[pektin|pectin]] run much faster. With acid such as buttermilk or yoghurt it forms gas bubbles that raise batter.
faustregeln: Pinches, not spoons: too much tastes soapy.
For crisp roast potatoes: about ½ tsp baking soda per 2 litres of par-boiling water. The surface turns rough and browns better.
Baking soda needs acid to raise; baking powder brings its own.

rolle.rolle: softens the edges of vegetables and potatoes
